title: Factors that influence the Outcome following transcatheter mitral valve interventions
summary:
Transcatheter heart valve interventions were initially performed primarily in inoperable patients and patients at very high surgical risk. In recent years, the indications for transcatheter valve interventions have progressively expanded. Despite increasing clinical experience with and utilization of transcatheter heart valve interventions, scientific evidence regarding transcatheter mitral valve interventions (TMVI) remains limited. In particular, there is a lack of evidence regarding post-interventional management and factors associated with outcomes following mitral valve interventions. To date, transcatheter mitral valve interventions are predominantly performed at specialized centers.

The aim of this exploratory analysis is to generate new insights based on existing clinical data (retrospective part of the study) and data collected as part of routine clinical care (prospective part of the study), with the goal of improving outcomes following transcatheter mitral valve interventions. A further objective is to identify relevant predictors associated with an increased procedural risk, thereby providing a stronger scientific basis for treatment strategy and clinical decision-making.

For the retrospective part of the study, routinely collected clinical data from patients who underwent TMVI will be retrospectively analyzed. No additional diagnostic, therapeutic, or other study-specific procedures are required.

Patients undergoing TMVI after ethics committee approval who are eligible for inclusion in the prospective part of the study will not undergo any additional diagnostic or therapeutic procedures beyond those performed as part of routine clinical care for TMVI. Only data generated during routine clinical care will be analyzed. Patients considered for inclusion after ethics committee approval will receive written and verbal information about study participation and will provide written informed consent prior to enrollment.
